original_value: We propose a deep-learning framework to detect and categorize oil spills in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images at a large scale. Through a carefully designed neural network model for image segmentation trained on an extensive dataset, we obtain state-of-the-art performance in oil spill detection, achieving results that are comparable to results produced by human operators. We also introduce a classification task, which is novel in the context of oil spill detection in SAR. Specifically, after being detected, each oil spill is also classified according to different categories of its shape and texture characteristics. The classification results provide valuable insights for improving the design of services for oil spill monitoring by world-leading providers. Finally, we present our operational pipeline and a visualization tool for large-scale data, which allows detection and analysis of the historical occurrence of oil spills worldwide.

result.paraphrase: We present a deep-learning framework for large-scale detection and categorization of oil spills in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery. Using a carefully designed image-segmentation neural network trained on a large dataset, the method delivers state-of-the-art oil spill detection performance comparable to human operators. We also propose a novel classification task for SAR oil-spill detection: once an oil spill is identified, it is assigned to categories based on shape and texture characteristics. The resulting classifications offer useful guidance for improving oil-spill monitoring services from world-leading providers. In addition, we describe our operational pipeline and a large-scale visualization tool that supports detection and analysis of the historical global occurrence of oil spills.
